record.prompt: Please run scripts/cost.sh on data/orders-2026-10.tsv and tell me the total shipping cost for October. Don't edit the script or data/zone-rates.tsv.

base_changes.keywords: cost.sh zone-rates CRLF no rate for zone
base_changes.content: scripts/cost.sh fails with 'no rate for zone "north"' because data/zone-rates.tsv has CRLF line endings (zone keys end in \r). User said not to edit the script or the rates file; workaround: pass a CR-stripped temp copy as the optional 2nd arg: tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > $t; scripts/cost.sh ORDERS $t.

User said not to edit the script or the rates file; workaround: pass a CR-stripped temp copy as the optional 2nd arg: tr -d '\\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv > \$t; scripts/cost.sh ORDERS \$t."

record.final_answer:
**The total shipping cost for October is 58.01.**

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |

The script failed the first time with `no rate for zone "north"`. The cause is that `data/zone-rates.tsv` has Windows (CRLF) line endings, so each zone name ends in a hidden `\r` and never matches the order file. To get around it without changing either file, I made a temporary copy of the rates with the `\r` characters removed and passed it as the script's optional second argument. I deleted the copy afterwards, and the repo has no changes.

To fix this permanently, convert `zone-rates.tsv` to LF line endings or make the script strip `\r`. I left both alone as you asked. I also saved this problem and the workaround to long-term memory for future sessions.
